The '''1993 Football Association Charity Shield''' was the 71st [[FA Community Shield|FA Charity Shield]], an annual [[Association football|football]] match played between the winners of the previous season's [[Premier League]] and [[FA Cup]] competitions. It was held at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] on 7 August 1993. The match was played between [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], who beat [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] to win the [[1993 FA Cup Final]], and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], champions of the [[1992–93 FA Premier League|inaugural Premier League competition]]. Watched by a crowd of 66,519, Manchester United won the Shield 5–4 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]], after the match had finished at 1–1 after 90 minutes. This was the second edition to have penalties to decide the winners. The first being 1974 when Liverpool beat Leeds United on penalties.

This was Arsenal's 12th's Charity Shield appearance and Manchester United's 17th. The 1993 staging of the event was the first to feature players wearing permanent squad numbers; this became common practise in time for the [[1993–94 in English football|1993–94]] season. [[Roy Keane]] made his debut for Manchester United in the match; he partnered [[Paul Ince]] in midfield. United began the match the brighter of the two teams and scored after eight minutes of play, through [[Mark Hughes]]. Striker [[Eric Cantona]] spurned two chances to extend United's lead, by which point Arsenal's midfield started to assert themselves. Five minutes before the interval, [[Ian Wright]] capitalised on a mistake by [[Ryan Giggs]] to score the equaliser. Arsenal started the second half strongly, which prompted Ferguson to tweak his formation and bring on [[Bryan Robson]] in place of Giggs. [[Eddie McGoldrick]] came on for his Arsenal debut in the 74th minute, and two minutes later, United were denied a penalty after Ince was brought down by [[John Jensen]].

As there were no further goals, the match was decided by a penalty shoot-out. Wright and [[Denis Irwin]] missed their penalties; the decisive penalty, taken by Arsenal goalkeeper [[David Seaman]], was saved by his opposite number, [[Peter Schmeichel]]. Arsenal manager [[George Graham (footballer, born 1944)|George Graham]] admitted his surprise over how the game was decided and thought both clubs would share the trophy; his counterpart [[Alex Ferguson]], though delighted with his team's victory, felt the [[Sudden death (sport)|sudden death]] aspect was unnecessary.

==Background==
The [[FA Community Shield|FA Charity Shield]] was founded in 1908 as a contest between the top professional and amateur teams of each season. It was played between the [[The Football League|Football League]] champions and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time in 1921; the formation of a new top-tier division, the [[Premier League]], in 1992 meant it displaced the Football League spot.<ref name="hist">{{cite news |title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=21 May 2016}}</ref> [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] acted as the home venue of the Shield, first hosting the event in 1974.<ref name="hist"/> The Arsenal players in the 1993 staging of the Charity Shield were the first in the competition's history to wear permanent [[squad number (association football)|squad numbers]] and names on the back of their shirts, while the Manchester United players used the traditional 1–11 numbering system without the names, which was phased out by the start of the [[1993–94 FA Premier League]] season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Playing by squad numbers sows seeds of confusion |first=David |last=Lacey |page=15 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=21 August 1993}}</ref> The Premier League intended to introduce persistent squad numbers with names at the start of the 1992–93 season, but [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] vetoed plans as their laundry room "was too small to handle all the extra shirts".<ref>{{cite news |title=Thomas on the high road back |first=Martin |last=Thorpe |page=15 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=21 August 1993 }}</ref>

Arsenal qualified for the 1993 FA Charity Shield by defeating [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] in a replay match of the [[1993 FA Cup Final]] to win the cup.<ref name="post"/> The club therefore completed a [[Double (association football)#Domestic Cup Double|domestic cup double]]; earlier in the season they beat Sheffield Wednesday 2–1 to win the [[1993 Football League Cup Final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arsenal.com/history/grahams-glory-years/gunners-clinch-fa-and-league-cup-double |title=Gunners clinch FA and League Cup double |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=16 December 2008 |access-date=16 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013093804/http://www.arsenal.com/history/grahams-glory-years/gunners-clinch-fa-and-league-cup-double |archive-date=13 October 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The other Charity Shield place went to Manchester United, winners of the [[1992–93 FA Premier League|inaugural Premier League]] competition.<ref name="post">{{cite news |title=Scots with little room for charity |first=Russell |last=Thomas |page=19 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=7 August 1993}}</ref> It was their first league title in 26 years and goalkeeper [[Peter Schmeichel]] felt the signing of striker [[Eric Cantona]] was a factor in the team's success: "He has added an element of surprise, imagination, inventiveness."<ref>{{cite news |title=United claim the glittering prize at last |first=Peter |last=Ball |page=19 |newspaper=The Times |date=3 May 1993}}</ref>

This was Manchester United's first appearance in the Charity Shield in three years; prior to this event they won 10 Shields outright ([[1908 FA Charity Shield|1908]], [[1911 FA Charity Shield|1911]], [[1952 FA Charity Shield|1952]], [[1956 FA Charity Shield|1956]], [[1957 FA Charity Shield|1957]], [[1983 FA Charity Shield|1983]]), shared four ([[1965 FA Charity Shield|1965]], [[1967 FA Charity Shield|1967]], [[1977 FA Charity Shield|1977]], [[1990 FA Charity Shield|1990]]) and lost three ([[1948 FA Charity Shield|1948]], [[1963 FA Charity Shield|1963]], [[1985 FA Charity Shield|1985]]). By contrast, Arsenal won seven previous Shields ([[1930 FA Charity Shield|1930]], [[1931 FA Charity Shield|1931]], [[1933 FA Charity Shield|1933]], [[1934 FA Charity Shield|1934]], [[1938 FA Charity Shield|1938]], 1948, [[1953 FA Charity Shield|1953]]), shared one with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in [[1991 FA Charity Shield|1991]] and lost four ([[1935 FA Charity Shield|1935]], [[1936 FA Charity Shield|1936]], [[1979 FA Charity Shield|1979]], [[1989 FA Charity Shield|1989]]).<ref name="jam">{{cite web |first=James |last=Ross |title=List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation (RSSSF) |date=15 August 2013 |access-date=11 January 2014}}</ref> Both clubs had only once met before in the Shield, when Arsenal won by four goals to three in 1948.<ref name="jam"/>

==Pre-match==
Both managers approached the match with a view to win, in spite of the Shield's friendly feel.<ref name="mil">{{cite news |title=Arsenal should aim to please |first=David |last=Miller |page=30 |newspaper=The Times |date=7 August 1993}}</ref> Arsenal manager [[George Graham (footballer, born 1944)|George Graham]] opined "Winning is a good habit, so why not start early?"<ref name="mil"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Tunnel of hate |pages=26–7 |newspaper=Daily Mirror|location=London |date=7 August 1993}}</ref> Graham lambasted those who found his team's playing style tedious: "The criticism that we don't pass the ball and we don't have flair is overdone. We won two championships and in the second lost one game out of 38."<ref>{{cite news |title=Glasgow glitter boys on parade |first=Steve |last=Curry |pages=78–9 |newspaper=Daily Express |location=London |date=7 August 1993}}</ref> However, Manchester United manager [[Alex Ferguson]] said "Winning means keeping your job, and it can be a delicate situation. But I tell myself I'm not going to fail in this game." Ferguson spoke in glowing terms of new signing [[Roy Keane]], a midfielder who gave United "unbelievable options, a real edge to the squad".<ref>{{cite news |title=Keane widens the horizons |first=Russell |last=Thomas |page=19 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=7 August 1993}}</ref>

The match was scheduled for a 12:30pm kick off since [[Sky Sports]] televised the match in both Scotland and England; they were unable to pick an afternoon slot because of the [[English football on television#3pm "Blackout"|television blackout]], which aimed to protect Scottish attendances.<ref name="sun">{{cite news |title=Wright kicks off with a screamer and a howler |first=Deryk |last=Brown |page=S2 |newspaper=The Sunday Times |location=London |date=8 August 1993}}</ref> [[UEFA]] warned [[The Football Association]] in the lead-up to the Charity Shield that a 3pm kick-off would result in a minimum fine of £5&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news |first=Bob |last=Harris |title=TV in Charity Shield shocker |page=64 |newspaper=Sunday Mirror |location=London |date=30 May 1993}}</ref> Deryk Brown of ''[[The Sunday Times]]'' wrote of the decision: "So, at least, the season is beginning as it will go on, at the mercy of television."<ref name="sun"/> Tickets for the game were advertised at a cost of between [[Pound sterling|£]]10 and £30.<ref>{{cite news |title=Display ad 26 |page=A15 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=6 August 1993}}</ref>

==Match==

===Team selection===
Arsenal lined up in a [[Formation (association football)#4–4–2|4–4–2]] formation; [[Eddie McGoldrick]] was included in the matchday squad, while [[Kevin Campbell (footballer)|Kevin Campbell]] partnered [[Ian Wright]] up front.<ref name="times"/> Ferguson deployed a [[Formation (association football)#4–2–4|4–2–4]] formation, with [[Paul Ince]] partnering debutant Keane in the midfield two.<ref name="times">{{cite news |title=Resilient Arsenal dip United's wings |first=Peter |last=Ball |page=20 |newspaper=The Times |date=9 August 1993}}</ref> [[Andrei Kanchelskis]] was picked in favour of [[Lee Sharpe]] on the right wing.<ref name="indy">{{cite news|title=United learning to live with their riches: Ferguson says he would have happily shared the spoils at Wembley |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football--charity-shield-united-learning-to-live-with-their-riches-ferguson-says-he-would-have-happily-shared-the-spoils-at-wembley-1460128.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football--charity-shield-united-learning-to-live-with-their-riches-ferguson-says-he-would-have-happily-shared-the-spoils-at-wembley-1460128.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |first=Joe |last=Lovejoy |newspaper=The Independent|location=London |date=9 August 1993 |access-date=6 January 2014}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

===Summary===
Manchester United began the first half the better of the two teams and led from the eighth minute.<ref name="sun"/> [[Denis Irwin]]'s cross into Arsenal's [[penalty area]] found [[Eric Cantona]] on the right side; he lobbed the ball in [[Mark Hughes]]' direction, who was surrounded by the Arsenal defenders.<ref name="sun"/> Hughes instinctively made a connection with the ball with an overhead shot that beat goalkeeper [[David Seaman]] at the near post.<ref name="sun"/> United fashioned another chance to score moments after; Keane fed the ball to Cantona whose shot was blocked by Seaman.<ref name="guardian"/><ref name="sun"/> Kanchelskis created a further chance for Cantona; the Frenchman's effort once more was denied, this time by an Arsenal defender.<ref name="guardian"/> "These proved costly misses", opined [[Patrick Barclay]], given United's tempo weakened, and Arsenal's [[John Jensen]] and [[Paul Davis (footballer born 1961)|Paul Davis]] started to impose themselves in midfield.<ref name="guardian"/> United captain [[Steve Bruce]] coped well against Campbell and Wright, but the latter striker equalised for Arsenal in the 40th minute.<ref name="guardian"/> A loose pass from [[Ryan Giggs]] was headed-on by Davis and the ball fell to Wright.<ref name="sun"/> He, "some 20 yards out", hit the ball first time, which dipped past the underside of the crossbar.<ref name="sun"/>

A tackle by Ince on [[Lee Dixon]] left the Arsenal defender with a damaged ankle; he came off at half time and was replaced by [[Martin Keown]].<ref name="indys">{{cite news |title=United have the last laugh in lottery |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-united-have-the-last-laugh-in-lottery-1459801.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-united-have-the-last-laugh-in-lottery-1459801.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |first=Norman |last=Fox |newspaper=The Independent on Sunday |location=London |date=8 August 1993}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Arsenal's performance improved after Wright's goal; [[Paul Merson]], a quiet figure in the first half, influenced their play in the second.<ref name="indys"/> Ferguson responded to Arsenal's newfound impetus by substituting Giggs for [[Bryan Robson]].<ref name="times"/> This tweaked United's formation to [[Formation (association football)#4–3–3|4–3–3]]; in spite of Ince's well-rounded performance, his partner Keane started to tire as the game went on and United's game therefore suffered.<ref name="guardian"/><ref name="times"/> Keane was shifted onto the right to accommodate Robson, who brought control to United's play.<ref name="guardian"/> In the meantime, [[Nigel Winterburn]] prevented Cantona from scoring, following good play by Kanchelskis.<ref name="guardian"/> Arsenal's service to Wright and Campbell was infrequent throughout the second half, but both players tested Schmeichel in goal.<ref name="guardian"/> McGoldrick came on for his Arsenal debut in the 74th minute, a versatile player, able to "sweep, score from midfield or play wide".<ref name="sun"/> Two minutes later, Seaman denied Keane from scoring with a one-handed save.<ref name="guds">{{cite news |title=Shoot-out spoils Shield's sweet charity |first=David |last=Lacey |page=12 |newspaper=The Guardian|location=London |date=9 August 1993}}</ref> United continued to attack and a move was broken down after Jensen's tackle brought Ince down in the Arsenal's penalty area.<ref name="guardian"/> [[Gerald Ashby]] refused to award a penalty – "the referee's decision otherwise was not supported by television replays".<ref name="guardian"/>

No further goals meant the game was decided on a penalty shoot-out. The first four penalties were scored – Ince and Bruce for United and Winterburn and Jensen for Arsenal, before Seaman saved Irwin's effort. Wright missed his penalty, prompting jeers from the United supporters.<ref name="sun"/> The shoot-out proceeded to [[Sudden death (sport)#Association football|sudden death]]; Robson scored and Seaman "saw his gentle penalty saved by his opposite number" to give United a 5–4 win and thereby the Shield.<ref name="sun"/>

==Post-match==
The Charity Shield was presented to Bruce by former Arsenal manager [[Billy Wright (footballer born 1924)|Billy Wright]].<ref>{{cite AV media |people=Keys, Richard (presenter), Tyler, Martin (commentator) |title=The Charity Shield: Arsenal v Manchester United |time=14:00:00–14:30:00 |publisher=Sky Sports |medium=Television production |date=7 August 1993 }}</ref> Wright died barely a year later, aged 70.<ref>{{cite news |title=Billy Wright |page=17 |newspaper=The Times |date=5 September 1994}}</ref> Graham assumed both clubs would share the trophy, so when it came to a penalty shoot-out he entrusted his players to decide their order.<ref name="werea">{{cite news |title=We're a mess |first=Mark |last=Irwin |page=56 |newspaper=Sunday Mirror |location=London |date=8 August 1993}}</ref> He described Wright's goal as "brilliant" and felt it was "unfortunate" that Seaman missed: "For a goalkeeper, he normally takes great penalties. He normally hits them hard but he decided to try and place this one and it didn't work."<ref name="werea"/> Wright was unashamed of his penalty miss, "...just as long as I don't do it when it is important".<ref>{{cite news |title=Top gun can grab 50 goals |first=Nigel |last=Clarke |page=33 |newspaper=Daily Mirror|location=London |date=9 August 1993}}</ref>

Ferguson remarked the Shield should not have been settled on penalties; to him it was a "celebration of success", though ultimately he was delighted his team won.<ref name="indy"/> He was pleased with the team's start – "I thought in the first 25 minutes we were really good and could have tied the match up then"<ref name="werea"/> – and considered lining the team up in a 4–3–3 formation to begin with, though wanted to see "how Keane played with Ince, what the balance was like".<ref name="times"/> Ince believed he should have been awarded a penalty after Jensen fouled him: "I was past their last man and there was no way I would have dived from there."<ref name="werea"/>
